note: Triennial election of the Banbridge rural district council, 1933; polling day for Co. Down, Thursday 25 May 1933. No contest: only nine nominations were received for the twenty divisions, and the nine 'together with the other sitting members are deemed to be re-elected' (Banbridge Chronicle, 29 April 1933, p. 5); the Belfast News-Letter (27 April 1933, p. 16) says the nominations make no change in the composition of the council. The paper names the nine without divisions; their divisions are taken from the 1930 return. The members deemed re-elected in the divisions with no nomination are recorded from reports of the council's meetings early in the term (Banbridge Chronicle), each with its division from the previous return or from the co-option report naming the predecessor (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 3 May 1930 return (J. E. Bailey, Crossgare); the Banbridge Chronicle meeting report cited names the member as sitting early in the term. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
